value.text:
A grep for `store.Memo` will match related structs such as `store.MemoRelation` and `store.MemoShare` because `Memo` is a prefix of those names. The search needs to be refined to avoid false positives.

The exact match pattern `store\.Memo\b` avoids false positives from related structs. `user_service_stats.go` returns `*store.Memo` via `ListMemos`, so any field changes there would require review.

Listing packages is cleaner than individual file paths. The main store package and its sqlite and mysql subpackages likely contain the struct definition and direct references.

Additional packages requiring review include the postgres database driver, store test utilities, API v1 routes and tests, RSS router, frontend tests, notification service, and memopayload runner. Proto-generated files were also checked; the generated `storepb.Memo` is a separate type from `store.Memo`.

Generated protobuf files should be excluded from the review list. The matches in store/memo_relation.go and store/memo_share.go need verification to confirm they reference the Memo struct directly.

// Visibility is the type of a visibility.
type Visibility string

const (
	// Public is the PUBLIC visibility.
	Public Visibility = "PUBLIC"
	// Protected is the PROTECTED visibility.
	Protected Visibility = "PROTECTED"
	// Private is the PRIVATE visibility.
	Private Visibility = "PRIVATE"
)

func (v Visibility) String() string {
	switch v {
	case Public:
		return "PUBLIC"
	case Protected:
		return "PROTECTED"
	default:
		return "PRIVATE"
	}
}

type Memo struct {
	// ID is the system generated unique identifier for the memo.
	ID int32

	UID string

	CreatorID int32
	CreatedTs int64

	// Domain specific fields
	Content    string
	Visibility Visibility
	Pinned     bool

	// Composed fields
	ParentUID *string
}

	ID  *int32

	switch v {

value.text:
The store layer explicitly deletes memo_relation and attachments before the memo row itself. The SQL-level ON DELETE CASCADE on memo_share is not the store layer's action.

Comment memos are deleted by the API layer first, not the store layer. The store layer itself deletes memo_relations and attachments before the memo row. This logic lives in store/memo.go.

q16.
memo_relation records (this memo as source or target), then attachments

`store.DeleteMemo` in `store/memo.go` deletes those first, then the `memo` row. The API `DeleteMemo` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` removes comment memos first; it does not have the store delete reactions or shares before the row (shares can cascade in SQL).

value.text:
The MySQL `GetUser` method belongs to the dialect DB driver, not `Store.GetUser`. If `Store.GetUser` is merely a wrapper, changing its signature would not require updating the dialect `GetUser`.

Store.GetUser is called by several production services. Authenticator methods in server/auth/authenticator.go are two call sites. EmailDispatcher in server/notification/email.go is two call sites. RSS service in server/router/rss/rss.go is one call site. FileServerService.getUserByUsername in server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go is one call site. APIV1Service.fetchCurrentUser in server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go is one call site. APIV1Service.SignIn in server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go is one call site.

APIV1Service.GetInstanceAdmin in server/router/api/v1/instance_service.go is one call site. SSO helpers in server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go are two call sites. ResolveUserByName in server/router/api/v1/user_resource_name.go is one call site. Store.GetUserByPATHash in store/user_setting.go is another call site. Tests in store/test/user_test.go, store/test/user_delete_test.go, store/demo_seed_test.go, and various API v1 tests also call it.

Frontend tests, attachment code, and store test files such as user_identity may also call Store.GetUser. SQLite and Postgres UpdateUser methods call d.GetUser directly on the driver instead.

value.description: Read CEL filter engine and dialect SQL conversion

value.text:
The engine is CEL (Common Expression Language) via google/cel-go, living in internal/filter/engine.go.

CEL compiles to a dialect-agnostic condition tree. That tree renders to SQL via AppendConditions or CompileToStatement for SQLite, MySQL, and Postgres. Each dialect appends the resulting WHERE clause in its ListMemos implementation.

q25.
CEL (`google/cel-go`) — internal/filter; each dialect’s `ListMemos` calls `filter.AppendConditions`, which compiles the CEL string to a condition tree and renders dialect-specific SQL (`DialectSQLite` / `DialectMySQL` / `DialectPostgres`) into the query `WHERE` clause.

The API validates the filter with `validateFilter` in `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go` (used from `ListMemos` in `memo_service.go`). Rendering is in `internal/filter/render.go` and `helpers.go`; dialect call sites are `store/db/sqlite/memo.go`, `store/db/mysql/memo.go`, and `store/db/postgres/memo.go`.

value.text:
The frontend auth interceptor lives in `web/src/connect.ts` as `authInterceptor`. It manages an access token (JWT Access Token V2) stored in localStorage and sent as `Authorization: Bearer`.

A refresh token lives in an HttpOnly cookie named `memos_refresh` and is sent via `credentials: include` on the `refreshToken` RPC. The backend package that validates these tokens is `server/auth` (its `Authenticator`).

q29.
web/src/connect.ts; access JWT (Bearer / localStorage) and refresh JWT (HttpOnly cookie); server/auth

`authInterceptor` in `connect.ts` attaches `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` and, on 401 or expiry, calls `refreshToken` with `credentials: "include"`. Access tokens live in `web/src/auth-state.ts`; refresh tokens are the `memos_refresh` cookie set by `auth_service_session.go`. The backend `server/auth` `Authenticator` validates Access Token V2, refresh tokens, and PATs.

Two memo lifecycle events are identified so far. Created dispatches to `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` for `memos.memo.created`. Updated dispatches to `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` for `memos.memo.updated`.

Deleted dispatches to `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` for `memos.memo.deleted`. Comment created dispatches to `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` for `memos.memo.comment.created`. All four events converge on `webhook.PostAsync` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. Created, updated, and deleted route through `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` before calling `PostAsync`. Comment created calls `PostAsync` directly.

The first three live in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` and go through `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (`memos.memo.created` / `.updated` / `.deleted`). Comment created uses the same file and posts `memos.memo.comment.created`. All four enqueue via `webhook.PostAsync`.
